Direct shear test on RSM-b soil at relative density 1.0; apparatus: direct shear (University of Notre Dame); loading: normal load 6.6 psi. Recorded: horizontal load vs horizontal motion (markers only).

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
The numbers below were digitized from the published figure by two readings made separately; they agree within the stated reading bounds at 15 of the 16 points, and the rest were settled against the scan. Student reviewers have looked at 6 of the 16 points on the scan; two reviewers confirmed all of them (see the provenance page). The test setup is incomplete: specimen height, normal stress, held constant, displacement rate are not reported.
:::

## Data

![horizontal load (shear stress) against horizontal motion (shear displacement), SI units, this test in red and the other tests printed in Fig. C-7B in gray. Error bars are reading bounds (half-widths from the digitization), not standard deviations. Filled markers were agreed by both readings, hollow ones were not.](../img/plots/b68-ds-fc-7b-n6p6psi.png){.lightbox}

Peak horizontal load (shear stress) 69.2 kPa at 1.02 mm horizontal motion (shear displacement); 45.0 kPa at 6.34 mm, the end of the record.

Download: [observations.csv](../files/data/experiments/b68-ds-fc-7b-n6p6psi/observations.csv) (16 points: 16 plotted symbols, 0 samples of the drawn curve; columns `x_si`, `y_si` with bounds `x_bound_si`, `y_bound_si`; panel 1: horizontal load (shear stress) in Pa against horizontal motion (shear displacement) in m; the printed-unit values, the pixel position on the scan and the review status of each point are kept in further columns) and [series.json](../files/data/experiments/b68-ds-fc-7b-n6p6psi/series.json) (units, conversion factors, how the points were read).

Reading bounds on this figure (how far our reading of the printed figure may be off, not the uncertainty of the test): typical bound 12 micrometers in horizontal motion (shear displacement), 408 Pa in horizontal load (0.6 percent of the peak). Both independent readings agree within these bounds at 15 of the 16 points; the other 1 was settled against the scan (read by one reader and verified by the other, or decided between two readings). [Check the digitized points against the scan](../figures/index.qmd#check-fc-7b).
